slides.headline: Ring Gives Surveillance Room to Roam
slides.subheadline: Flying and wheeled cameras bring indoor mapping, cloud processing and privacy questions.

cards.title: Ring Rover Cam
cards.body: Wheeled autonomous security robot marketed for business.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use the publication palette throughout the storyboard. Place the headline above a schematic indoor outline. Branch a dashed airborne path toward an abstract drone glyph and a solid floor path toward an abstract rover glyph. Anchor each product caption at its path endpoint. Keep silhouettes conceptual, not dimensionally representative; reserve clear text zones.

slides.headline: Two Dates, Different Certainty
slides.subheadline: Rover shipping is scheduled; the drone still needs regulatory authorization.

cards.title: Ring Rover Cam
cards.body: Scheduled shipping; already available for preorder when the article was published.

cards.title: Ring Drone Cam
cards.body: Amazon's target depends on Federal Communications Commission authorization.

slides.svgBlueprint: Draw a horizontal release rail with two labeled milestones, explicitly not to scale. Use a solid square for Rover's scheduled shipping and a hollow accent circle for Drone's conditional target. Offset the captions above and below the rail. End the drone segment with a dashed line rather than a completion arrow.

slides.headline: Different Mapping, Shared Cloud Processing
slides.subheadline: AI Pilot combines device cameras, specialized vision models, on-device sensors and cloud processing.

cards.title: Ring Drone Cam
cards.body: Customers carry the drone through indoor spaces to map floor plans.

cards.title: Ring Rover Cam
cards.body: Autonomous exploration maps indoor floor plans.

slides.svgBlueprint: Draw two schematic floor plans without dimensions. Show a hand-and-drone symbol following a dotted setup path on the left; show a rover tracing its own exploration path on the right. Connect both diagrams to one cloud-processing node below. Avoid arrows implying specific uploads, retention or processing sequences not established by the dossier.

slides.headline: A Flying Camera's Viewing Envelope
slides.subheadline: Field of view, rotation and resolution describe what the onboard camera offers.
slides.svgBlueprint: Center an abstract camera lens inside a circular rotation arrow. Draw an accurately proportioned 148-degree viewing wedge in translucent accent. Place three numerical readouts around the perimeter with short, noncrossing leaders. Treat the wedge as an angular diagram, never a coverage-distance claim.

slides.headline: Eight Minutes, With Conditions Attached
slides.subheadline: Flight duration, navigation surfaces and subscriber access constrain the drone's promise.

cards.title: 8 minutes
cards.body: On a new, fully-charged battery under controlled conditions.

cards.title: Navigation may degrade near
cards.body: Polished marble, wet tile, featureless blank matte walls, frameless glass and mirrors.

cards.title: Amazon Ring Protect subscribers
cards.body: Set-route and scheduled operation described; subscription price not stated.

slides.svgBlueprint: Build three full-width bands separated by thin ink rules, not floating cards. Pair the runtime band with an unscaled battery outline; pair navigation with one abstract reflective-wall motif; pair subscription access with a route passing through a labeled gate. Keep each illustration small enough to preserve generous text width.

slides.headline: Rover Trades Flight for Floor Coverage
slides.subheadline: Amazon claims indoor coverage alongside high-resolution video and stationary scanning.

metrics.label: Up to video resolution
metrics.body: Livestreaming and recording while patrolling or scanning.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use a large schematic business floor plan as the upper field, explicitly not to scale. Place a rover glyph at a designated scan point with a complete circular sweep. Set three metrics in a single bottom rail. Do not shade the plan as guaranteed coverage or imply walls are transparent to the camera.

slides.headline: Rover Cannot Patrol Every Floor
slides.subheadline: Indoor, single-floor operation comes with explicit terrain exclusions.

cards.title: Incompatible terrain
cards.body: Curved edges, sunken areas and black glossy floors.

slides.svgBlueprint: Draw one continuous schematic floor section across the slide. Attach three callouts to a staircase, an abstract recessed glossy-floor segment and a raised transition. Mark incompatibilities with accent stop bars. Label only the transition with its supplied threshold; do not invent stair dimensions, robot clearance or terrain tolerances.

slides.headline: Recording Outlasts the Patrol
slides.subheadline: Rover cloud retention is specified; a separate drone retention period is not.

cards.title: Rover: up to 180 days
cards.body: Cloud-stored videos: doorbell rings, motion events and Live View events.

cards.title: Drone: retention not stated
cards.body: The supplied article gives no separate cloud video retention period.

slides.svgBlueprint: Create two full-width ledger rows. In the Rover row, place a cloud archive symbol beside a long retention bar labeled up to 180 days. In the Drone row, use an outlined document with an em dash, not a zero-length bar. Keep the rows visually distinct so missing information cannot be mistaken for zero retention.

slides.headline: Ring's Privacy Record Follows It Indoors
slides.subheadline: The FTC's earlier case concerned private recordings and safeguards against hackers.

metrics.label: FTC investigation
metrics.body: Ring charged with allowing employees and contractors to watch customers' private-space recordings.

metrics.label: US customer accounts
metrics.body: FTC said Ring's safeguards allowed hackers to access these accounts.

slides.svgBlueprint: Set the investigation year as a tall typographic spine on the left. Place the account count in a large right-side evidence block with its attribution directly underneath. Use a restrained document-outline motif and thin connecting rule. Do not depict these historical allegations as incidents involving the new robots.

slides.headline: Mobile Security, Unresolved Privacy Questions
slides.subheadline: Throw Away the Key Encryption arrived in September 2026; its protections remain contested.

cards.title: Amazon's assurance
cards.body: Amazon says Throw Away the Key Encryption will protect both devices' videos.

cards.title: EFF's assessment
cards.body: EFF says it remains well short of end-to-end encryption.

slides.svgBlueprint: Place the two attributed statements on opposing sides of a central abstract lock outline. Use an open bracket around the lock to signify an unresolved assessment, not a demonstrated vulnerability. Keep Amazon's statement in ink and EFF's challenge in accent. Give the closing headline a broad, uncluttered lower text zone.
